name: Horizon: Count Every Tiling
description: Ten boards with holes, from 4x4 to 10x12. The task: the exact number of ways to cover each board with dominoes, a count that grows from a couple of dozen to over a billion. It can be done by hand, column by column, but only by keeping perfect books over hundreds of partial patterns. Keys are computed by two different exact algorithms.
hook: Can it count a billion domino tilings without missing one?
author: Gauntlet Horizon

cases.prompt:
Here is a board with 4 rows and 4 columns. Squares marked # must be covered; squares marked . are holes and must stay uncovered.

####
####
###.
###.

A domino is a 1x2 tile that covers two squares sharing a side (it can lie horizontally or vertically). In how many different ways can the 14 marked squares be covered completely with 7 dominoes, with no overlaps, no domino on a hole and nothing sticking out of the board? Two coverings are different if some pair of squares is covered by one domino in one covering but not in the other.

Give the exact count as a single integer, all digits, with no spaces, commas or other separators.
cases.notes: [level 1] 4x4 board, 14 squares. Key by column-by-column transfer-matrix counting (Python, big integers), re-checked by an independent memoised first-empty-square search in JavaScript (verify.mjs). Horizon ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly more work than the one below. Every level is worth the same, so the test score is the share of the ladder climbed; the headline is the highest level solved reliably.
